tasks.short: Direct the HR team on hiring, pay, absence, and the works council.

today.trigger: The working day starts, or a site manager, a specialist, or the works council raises a problem.
steps: Check Teams, mail, and the Power BI dashboard for what moved overnight at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
Speak with the HR business partners about open roles, absence files, and shift cover.
Set the day's priorities for recruiters, payroll, learning, compensation, and the administrators.
Step into a case that is stuck: a hire, a Wet verbetering poortwachter deadline, a pay question, or an OR item.
Follow up on what was promised to a manager or the OR.
drudgery: Collecting the same status from twelve specialists.
Copying figures from Power BI into a note for the management team.
Chasing updates that already sit in AFAS or Recruitee.
today.time_sinks: Most of these hours are meetings, and a large slice before each meeting goes to finding out where the work stands.

lenses.faster: About half an hour of morning chasing through Teams, mail, Recruitee, and the dashboard disappears on a normal day. The stand-up and the 1:1s stay at their current length, and editing the exception list takes about fifteen minutes.
lenses.autonomous: It starts at 07:30 on working days, and again when a value-stream measure slips, such as onboarding still open after week one or a Wet verbetering poortwachter deadline inside two weeks. The exception list builds on its own; the director sets priorities and gates before anyone acts on it.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made every week, where today it waits for the quarterly HR plan: how to redeploy the twelve specialists when one site's hiring or absence slips. Demand from the three site managers would grow if the list were cheap, because each would ask for a mid-week shift of HR time whenever a peak or a sick wave hits.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the morning status chase. The work to keep is the 1:1 when a specialist is stuck, and the preparation with the works council.
lenses.options: Three priority lists for the same week, one protecting week-one onboarding, one clearing Wet verbetering poortwachter deadlines, and one filling open warehouse roles, stop different work. Choosing the list is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The week starts from an exception list, and more of it goes to difficult 1:1s and to writing down gates before any aid runs. The director gains the right to decide, with the works council where consent is required, which HR steps may proceed and which wait for a person each time. The job becomes more expert in how the team is run, and the progress-chasing shrinks.
reach: The HR Business Partner's Monday note for one site, once the director knows that site's shift pattern and the Wet verbetering poortwachter dates already stored in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: The director stays accountable for the twelve specialists and for what HR promises the works council. A list cannot tell that a recruiter has lost a hiring manager's trust, and it cannot hold that conversation or an OR dispute.
tasks.pattern_why: The day's priorities depend on people and on the OR, so the director has to stay the lead. A fixed report can gather the exceptions; it cannot direct the team. An agent that assigned the work would need a gate on every item and would still be the heavier design.

in_practice.trigger: Each working day at 07:30, and again when onboarding is still open after week one, a role passes the team's own time-to-hire mark, or a Wet verbetering poortwachter deadline falls inside two weeks.
steps: Overnight, a report lists exceptions from Recruitee, AFAS, and Studytube for Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo.
The director edits that list into priorities for the twelve specialists.
In the 1:1s the director handles what the list cannot see: a strained manager relationship, an OR concern, a sensitive case.
When someone proposes that an aid take a step alone, the director records the gate and whether the OR must be asked first.
The director names who acts on each exception before the list is shared with the team.
in_practice.human_gate: The director sets the day's priorities and any gate. The report does not assign work, close a case, or write to a manager or the OR.
data_needed: Open roles and stage from Recruitee
Absence cases and contract end dates from AFAS, without medical notes
Certificate expiry from Studytube
The measures the director already uses: time to hire, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, verzuim
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint list on the HR site, one row per exception, with the director's name and the person who will act.

evidence.claim: Workday's autopilot agents let a customer decide which tasks run alone, which need review, and which a person decides. Actions are logged with the approver, and candidate outreach waits for a recruiter.
Commentary on the same October 2026 launch treats managing agents as a new HR job, which is the extra work this director would take on when setting gates.
Reported IBM practice is that agents can recommend a pay increase while the manager decides, because accountability stays with a person.
The works council discusses AI policy in the article 24 meeting, and one decision can require both advice and consent.

risks: A clean list hides a case that is going badly and that nobody has typed into AFAS or Recruitee.
If specialists believe the director already sees every queue, they stop escalating early.
Skipping the article 24 discussion, or ignoring a consent right, stops the rollout, and gate-and-log review grows with every new aid.
research_questions: Over two ordinary weeks, how many hours does the director spend gathering status, and how many in 1:1s and OR preparation?
How often is the underlying AFAS or Recruitee status already wrong, so that a morning list would mislead the stand-up?
Which items on that list would the works council treat as monitoring or task allocation that needs advice or consent?
Do the twelve specialists still raise a stuck case when they believe the director already sees their queue?

tasks.short: Advise managers on policy, equal treatment, and harassment, and on what should change.

today.trigger: A manager asks what the policy or a CAO allows, often after an incident or before a talk with an employee.
steps: Ask what happened, which site, which shift, and whether the person is own staff or flex.
Look up the SharePoint policy and the article in the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO.
Check AFAS for contract type and function group, and keep medical notes out of the mail.
Talk the manager through what they may do, and escalate harassment or conflict the same day.
Recommend a policy change when the same question keeps coming back.
drudgery: Answering the same leave, allowance, and roster questions several times a week.
Searching SharePoint for the current version of a policy.
Rewriting a CAO article in plain Dutch for each manager.
today.time_sinks: Finding the current clause and writing it out again takes the repeatable time; a harassment or conflict conversation then takes as long as the people need.

lenses.faster: Finding the clause and writing the first answer shrinks from about half an hour to a ten-minute check of the quotation. A harassment, discrimination, or conflict conversation stays as long as it takes, often an hour or more, with a person in the room.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a manager or supervisor sends a question by Teams or mail, from any site. Retrieval and a Dutch draft run on their own for a routine question; an HR Business Partner or the director approves the text before it is sent. Sensitive cases bypass the draft and go straight to a named person.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors at Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo, and the on-site leads of the three staffing agencies, get a routine policy answer before the shift starts. They are unserved today because the HR business partners work days. Demand would grow if this were cheap: every shift supervisor would ask, and peak season would raise the volume with the flex pool.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss typing out the same leave and allowance answer. The work to keep is the conversation when someone reports harassment or a conflict, and the judgment that a policy itself should change.
lenses.options: Two drafts of the same question, one a strict reading of the transport CAO and one the local warehouse practice, lead the supervisor to do different things on the shift tonight. The approved wording is the decision.
lenses.altitude: Routine answers arrive as drafts with the clause attached, and the afternoons stay with cases about people. The director gains the right to decide which questions the desk may prepare and which must reach a named person the same day. Handbook time shrinks; judgment on conflict and on policy changes takes a larger share of the week, so the job becomes more expert.
reach: The HR Business Partner's written reply to a routine CAO or policy question, once the director and the HR business partners have listed the questions that must reach a person the same day.

tasks.human_edge: The director, with the HR business partner, judges credibility, safety, and what the company will do when the matter can become a complaint, a dismissal, or a Wet verbetering poortwachter file. Quoting the policy does not carry that accountability.
tasks.pattern_why: A routine question can need the transport CAO, the warehouse CAO, a SharePoint policy, and the contract type in AFAS, in an order that depends on the wording. One fixed call is too brittle, and a script cannot read the free text. The answer counts as HR's position only after a person approves it.

in_practice.trigger: A manager, a supervisor, or an agency lead on site sends a policy question by Teams or mail, including from the night shift.
steps: On arrival the question is classed as routine policy, or as harassment, discrimination, dismissal, or health.
Sensitive cases go straight to the HR business partner on duty and the director, on the existing human route.
For a routine question the desk opens the matching CAO article, the SharePoint policy, and the contract type in AFAS, without medical notes.
It drafts a Dutch answer that quotes the clause, says the draft was generated, and names the approver still required.
An HR business partner or the director approves, edits, or rejects, and the sent text keeps the disclosure and the approver's name.
The night-shift queue is cleared before 14:00 so the answer is waiting when the shift starts.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is sent as HR's answer until an HR business partner or the director approves the text. Harassment, discrimination, dismissal, and health questions are taken by a person the same day and are not answered as desk advice.
data_needed: The question in the sender's words
Current transport CAO and warehouse CAO texts
Current SharePoint policies
Contract type and function group from AFAS, excluding medical notes
in_practice.logs_to: The HR policy log in SharePoint: question, clauses cited, draft, approver, time sent, and whether the case was diverted to a person.

evidence.claim: IBM first cut dedicated HR support and closed HR mail and phone for about 21,000 managers, and internal NPS fell to -35. AskHR later reached CSAT +74 and handled 16 million messages in 2025. IBM's stated lesson was to take one small pain, make it good, and pilot.
At IBM India about 90 to 95 percent of HR questions go through an assistant. Agents recommend pay increases and managers decide; accountability stays with the person.
A Wipro recruitment agent mishandled one demographic group, and Wipro kept a parallel process while the vendor corrected it.

Chatbots and generated content must be disclosed. Employers must take AI-literacy measures. With more than 750 employees Noordhaven does not get the small mid-cap relief, and fines run up to 15 million euro or 3 percent of turnover.

risks: A wrong clause, approved in a hurry, is acted on by a night supervisor before anyone can correct it.
Closing the Teams or mail route before supervisors trust the desk repeats the failure IBM has already described.
A harassment or health question mis-classed as routine pulls special-category absence data into a prompt and produces advice a person should have given.
research_questions: What share of manager questions last quarter could be answered by quoting a CAO article or a SharePoint policy, with no further judgment?
How often does a question that looks routine on arrival become a complaint, a harassment case, or a Wet verbetering poortwachter file within a month?
Will night-shift supervisors act on an answer that arrived before the shift and was approved by a named person, and do they still need someone they can call that night?
Can the desk answer from the policy texts while keeping special-category absence data out of the prompt and the log?

tasks.short: Find causes of people problems in the figures and recommend a change in policy.

today.trigger: The monthly dashboard refresh, a spike in verzuim, or a request from the management team or the works council to explain a people problem.
steps: Open the Power BI dashboard on the nightly AFAS extract.
Export to Excel and split the figures by site and, where the data allows, by shift.
Ask the people analyst and the HR business partners what they think sits behind the movement.
Write a short recommendation on policy or practice.
Present it to the management team and, when it touches staff, prepare a version for the OR.
drudgery: Rebuilding the workbook when the export layout has changed.
Waiting while the people analyst reconciles AFAS corrections.
Stripping names out by hand before a pack can be shared.
today.time_sinks: Cleaning and reshaping the extract takes the hours, and the cause is discussed only after that.

lenses.faster: Rebuilding the export in Excel drops out of the month. Reading the scenario note and choosing a cause takes about an hour per site, where the old workbook took the best part of a day.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when the monthly Power BI refresh lands, and when 90-day retention or verzuim at one site moves past the band the director and the people analyst have already set. The notes draft themselves from the analyst's measures; the director picks the cause that will be acted on.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the works council: a monthly fact pack on verzuim and 90-day retention by site and shift, with no names, so the OR can check HR's story before it gives advice. Demand would grow if the pack were cheap, because the OR would ask for it at article 24 meetings and not only when a conflict is already open.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding the Excel export. The work to keep is sitting with a site manager and agreeing the cause.
lenses.options: Three cause notes for the same movement, hiring quality, shift design, and supervision, point to different fixes: who is hired, how the roster works, or a conversation with a manager. Picking the note is the decision.
lenses.altitude: The month becomes reading a few cause notes and testing one at a site. The director gains the right to send a signed cause, with the figures, to a site manager, and a names-free version to the OR. More of the task is judgment and less is extraction, so the expertise required goes up.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's first-cut note on what moved in 90-day retention and verzuim, once the director can read the measure definitions and spot a late AFAS correction.

tasks.human_edge: Naming a cause is a management act. The director knows which site manager will act on a finding and which finding would be unfair to a shift. The figures can line up; they cannot carry that conversation or sign the recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: The measures can be fixed in the people analyst's layer, and the director must stay the lead on the cause and the recommendation. One model call that emitted a single cause would hide the choice. An agent that wrote to managers or the OR would act before the judgment is made.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly Power BI refresh from the nightly AFAS extract, and any week when 90-day retention or verzuim at one site moves past the band already agreed with the people analyst.
steps: The people analyst's measures refresh from the nightly AFAS extract, at site and shift, with no employee names.
A copilot drafts three cause notes per site: hiring quality, shift design, and supervision, each tied to those figures.
The director deletes any note the extract cannot support.
The director picks one cause to test with the HR business partner and the site manager.
When the finding is a policy matter, a version with no employee-level rows is prepared for the OR, and the director decides whether to send it.
in_practice.human_gate: The director chooses the cause that will be acted on and signs anything that goes to a manager or the OR. The copilot does not write to them.
data_needed: Nightly AFAS extract
Agreed definitions of 90-day retention, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, and verzuim
Headcount by site and shift, aggregated
in_practice.logs_to: The people-analytics folder in SharePoint: the note, the figures it used, the refresh date of the extract, and the cause the director signed.

evidence.claim: A nightly AFAS extract into Power BI can show movements by site. It cannot by itself establish the cause, and corrections after the nightly refresh can reverse a month's story.
Monitoring and evaluation of workers sit in the high-risk list in the Commission draft of 19 May 2026, and a final human click does not take a tool that ranks people outside that list.
The works council discusses AI policy in the article 24 meeting, and one decision can require both advice and consent, which covers a pack the OR is asked to rely on.

risks: A cause note blames a shift or a supervisor because the nightly extract is incomplete or a correction lands the next week.
A pack that ranks managers or teams can fall under monitoring or evaluation from 2 December 2027, and a final click does not remove it.
Employee-level rows in an OR pack or in a prompt breach the AVG, and absence data is special category.
research_questions: Are 90-day retention and verzuim stable at site and shift in the nightly extract, or do AFAS corrections a week later reverse the story?
When a site manager is shown three cause notes, do they choose a different action from the one they would choose after a conversation with the HR business partner alone?
Will the OR accept a monthly pack with no employee-level rows, and does counsel agree it stays outside the AI Act's monitoring and evaluation category?

tasks.short: Plan hiring, training, and labour relations and keep that plan on track.

today.trigger: The yearly planning round, a peak-season preview from operations, or a date on the labour-relations calendar.
steps: Ask recruitment, learning, payroll, compensation, and the HR business partners for their plans.
Check Studytube for forklift, VCA, and food-safety certificates, and Recruitee for roles that will still be open.
Fit the plans onto the shift calendars at the three sites.
Reserve time with the OR and note the CAO dates, including the transport CAO end on 31 December 2026.
Publish the plan on SharePoint and correct it when the sites diverge.
drudgery: Chasing four plans and merging them in one deck or sheet.
Discovering late that a wave of certificate expiries clashes with a peak.
Updating a yearly document that is already behind the sites.
today.time_sinks: Merging specialist plans and discovering clashes late takes longer than the decision about what to pause.

lenses.faster: Rewriting the annual plan document each quarter drops out. The meeting that decides what pauses still takes about an hour, with a one-page picture already filled in from Studytube, Recruitee, and the CAO calendar.
lenses.autonomous: It starts on the first Monday of the month, and in any week when Studytube shows forklift, VCA, or food-safety certificates expiring within 60 days. The picture assembles itself; the director confirms the month's plan and the OR agenda.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made every month, where today it sits in the annual plan: which site gets the learning specialists and the recruiters before the next peak, based on certificates and open roles. Demand from the three site managers would grow if the picture were cheap, because each would ask for that capacity every month.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss merging four plans into a deck that is stale by March. The work to keep is the argument about what pauses when hiring, training, and the CAO calendar clash.
lenses.options: Two monthly plans, one moving the learning specialists onto expiring certificates and one keeping them on a longer programme, leave a different site short of certified people before peak. The director's pick changes what gets done.
lenses.altitude: The month starts from a one-page picture of hire-to-productive, hire-to-retire, absence-to-return, and the pay cycle. The director gains the right to move learning and recruiting time across Rotterdam, Tilburg, and Venlo during the year. The expertise shifts toward trade-offs between those streams.
reach: The Learning and Development Specialist's list of forklift, VCA, and food-safety certificates expiring within 60 days, once the director knows which certificates each site is required to hold.

tasks.human_edge: When training time, open roles, and the OR or CAO calendar collide, the director chooses what stops. The works council and the unions will hold the director to that choice. A picture of the clash does not make it.
tasks.pattern_why: The picture can be assembled from calendars and systems the company already has, and the director stays the lead on what pauses and on the OR agenda. An agent that moved trainers or changed an OR date would act on a labour-relations decision.

in_practice.trigger: The first Monday of the month, and any week Studytube shows forklift, VCA, or food-safety certificates expiring within 60 days.
steps: Pull training gaps from Studytube, open roles from Recruitee, and OR and CAO dates from the labour-relations calendar.
Draft a one-page picture of the four value streams and where they collide, including training hours against shift cover.
The director decides what pauses and tells learning, recruitment, and the HR business partners.
OR agenda items for the month are listed for the director to confirm with the OR chair.
The approved picture is filed, with the date, so the next month starts from it.
in_practice.human_gate: The director confirms the month's plan and the OR agenda. The draft does not move a person's training, shift, or vacancy.
data_needed: Certificate expiries and completions from Studytube
Open roles and stage from Recruitee
CAO and OR meeting dates
Peak weeks the operations team has already given HR
in_practice.logs_to: The monthly HR plan in SharePoint, with the director's approval and the date.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 can compute a match score for a vacancy and for internal talent. The partner page that describes it publishes no measured results, so a score in the hiring plan would be an unproven ranking.
Recruitment systems that rank candidates stay in the high-risk category even when a person clicks at the end. Moving CV data into fields without a score can fall outside it.
The works council discusses AI policy in the article 24 meeting, and one decision can require both advice and consent.

risks: The picture will keep being trusted after Studytube completions or Recruitee stages have lagged the floor.
Turning on the AFAS candidate match score inside this plan is a ranking tool, and a final click does not take it outside the recruitment rules.
Moving trainers between sites, when that changes training time or the work, can be an advice matter for the OR if it was not discussed.
research_questions: Which activities in last year's HR plan did not happen, and was the cause a stale document or a real clash with the shifts?
Does Studytube show forklift, VCA, and food-safety expiry early enough to move a trainer before peak?
Would site managers honour a monthly capacity decision, or would they still escalate around it to the director?

tasks.short: Prepare the personnel budget and keep spending inside it.

today.trigger: The annual budget calendar from finance, and the monthly personnel-cost variance the controller sends.
steps: Export positions, contracts, and salary data from AFAS.
Apply the transport CAO scales and the warehouse CAO scales in Excel, with employer charges.
Add flex costs from the three agency portals and from accounts payable.
Send the draft to the controller and explain the gaps.
Track spend through the year and approve changes that were not in the establishment.
drudgery: Rekeying scales and employer charges into Excel.
Matching agency invoices to hours ordered.
Explaining the same mapping to finance at every budget round.
today.time_sinks: Building the sheet takes longer than deciding what the company can afford.

lenses.faster: Rekeying positions, CAO scales, and employer charges into Excel drops out. Reviewing exceptions with the controller stays: about two hours in a normal month, and longer in the annual round.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when finance opens the annual budget, and each month when the controller opens the personnel-cost variance. The pack calculates itself from AFAS and the wage tables; the director approves it before it goes to the finance director.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the finance director and the controller: at each peak, a costed choice between extra flex hours and a fixed contract, split by site and by the two CAOs. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because operations would ask for that choice before every peak week, not only in the annual round.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rekeying scales into Excel. The work to keep is the conversation with the finance director about what the three sites can actually run.
lenses.options: Three packs for the same year, more flex, more fixed contracts, or fewer open roles, change the establishment the management team is asked to approve. Seeing them side by side is what makes the spend decision real.
lenses.altitude: Budget meetings start from a pack that already separates the two CAOs and the flex spend. The director gains the right to approve a flex-or-fixed cost choice with the controller without rebuilding the sheet. Less expertise sits in the arithmetic, and more sits in the trade-off the sheet cannot see.
reach: The FP&A Analyst's first commentary on the personnel-cost variance, once the director understands how employer charges and the three agencies' invoices meet the general ledger in AFAS.

tasks.human_edge: The director and the finance director still decide what the company will spend. A correct sheet cannot weigh a CAO increase against a promise already made to the OR, or tell a site it will run a peak with fewer people.
tasks.pattern_why: Own-staff cost follows written rules: AFAS positions, the two CAO wage tables, and the employer charges payroll already maintains. A small program can calculate that. A model adds nothing to the arithmetic. Late or messy agency files wait in an exception queue with the same rules once the file is in.

in_practice.trigger: The annual budget round, and each month when the controller opens the personnel-cost variance.
steps: A program reads filled positions, contract types, and salary scales from AFAS.
It applies the current transport CAO scales, the in-house warehouse CAO scales, and the employer charges the payroll specialist maintains.
It adds flex hours and rates from the three agency portals where those files have arrived.
It writes a pack that separates own staff from flex, and lists lines it could not price.
The director and the controller review exceptions: a new shift, a role outside the establishment, agency spend outside the rate card.
The director approves the pack before it goes to the finance director.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves each annual budget and each monthly variance pack. The program does not post to the general ledger.
data_needed: Positions, contract types, and scales in AFAS
Both CAO wage tables
Employer-charge rates maintained by payroll
Agency hours and invoices from the three portals
in_practice.logs_to: The finance budget folder in SharePoint: version, source files, exception list, and the director's approval.

evidence.claim: Own-staff pay for a Dutch employer on two known CAO wage tables can be calculated from positions, scales, and employer charges. Agency invoices are a separate feed and often lag the payroll close.

Workday's autopilot announcement covers finance as well as HR, with a customer-set choice of what runs alone and what a person approves, and with the approver stored on the action. That is a logged approval pattern; it is not a Dutch CAO calculator.

risks: A wrong CAO scale or employer-charge rate produces a pack that looks finished and is wrong.
Agency hours and invoices arrive on a different rhythm from the AFAS payroll close, so the flex half of the pack can be a month behind.
Approving the pack without reading the exception list hands the real spend decisions to the table.
research_questions: Can own-staff pay be reproduced from AFAS positions and the two CAO tables within a tolerance the controller will sign?
How many days after month end do the three agency invoices become usable, relative to the payroll close?
What share of personnel-budget lines are exceptions no table can price, such as a settlement, a new shift, or an allowance already promised to the OR?

tasks.short: Study new law, rulings, and both CAOs and judge the effect on Noordhaven.

today.trigger: A CAO update, a union or employer-association note, a change in absence law, or a question from payroll or the OR.
steps: Find the official text and the current protocol of the transport CAO or the warehouse CAO.
Read the changed articles against practice at the three sites, including flex on site.
Ask payroll and compensation what the change does to pay or to absence handling.
Write a note for the HR team and decide whether the OR should hear it, including in the article 24 slot.
File the note in SharePoint.
drudgery: Reading a long protocol to find the few articles that change an allowance or a certificate rule.
Checking an online summary against the signed text.
Rewriting the same note for the OR, for payroll, and for the site managers.
today.time_sinks: The reading and the cross-check against two CAOs take the hours; the decision at the end is short.

lenses.faster: Finding the changed articles drops from about half a day to a twenty-minute check that every quotation sits in the official text. Writing the note for payroll and the OR stays, and it is shorter because the brief is already in Dutch.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a new CAO protocol, an arbitration or court note, a Wet verbetering poortwachter change, or an EU AI Act change reaches the director, payroll, or compensation. One model call writes the brief; the director approves it before anyone treats it as HR's reading.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the works council and to the people who bargain the in-house warehouse CAO: one cited brief that prices a single union demand, starting with FNV's ask for worker zeggenschap over AI, before the transport CAO ends on 31 December 2026. Demand is high in this bargaining round. It falls between rounds, and it grows again when a union puts an AI clause on the table.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss reading a whole protocol to find three changed articles. The work to keep is the call on what Noordhaven will concede and what it will change on the floor.
lenses.options: Two briefs of the same text, one treating it as binding on both CAOs and one as binding only on the transport CAO, produce different bargaining positions and a different note to the OR. The checked reading is the decision.
lenses.altitude: When a text changes, the director's time goes to checking quotations and deciding who must act. The director gains a documented way to put an item on the article 24 agenda or on the CAO list while the text is still new. The expertise moves from searching to judging whether a reading is solid enough to act on.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first reading of a new wage table, once the director can tell a transport CAO scale from an in-house warehouse scale and can check a quotation against the signed text.

tasks.human_edge: The director decides what to concede in bargaining and whether a reading is solid enough to change a policy or a pay practice. A brief with a wrong citation, signed off in haste, becomes the company position. The director signs.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is one new text, and the checkable output is a short brief with quotations and source locations. That is a single model call inside a fixed path: store the text, draft, check quotations, approve. An agent is unnecessary because the path does not branch, and a script cannot read the legal prose.

in_practice.trigger: A new CAO protocol, an arbitration or court note, a change to the Wet verbetering poortwachter, or a change to the EU AI Act reaches the director, the payroll specialist, or the compensation specialist.
steps: The new text is stored next to the current transport CAO, the warehouse CAO, and the policies.
One model call returns a two-page brief: what changed, who it affects, and quotations with their location in the source.
The director checks each quotation against the official text and strikes anything that does not match.
The director decides whether HR acts, whether the OR must hear it under article 24, and whether it belongs in the 2027 CAO round.
Only the approved brief is filed for the team.
in_practice.human_gate: The director approves the brief before anyone treats it as HR's reading. No policy letter and no bargaining position is sent on the draft.
data_needed: The new official text
Current CAO texts and protocols
Current SharePoint policies
The open OR and bargaining items
in_practice.logs_to: The legal-and-CAO library in SharePoint: source file, brief, which quotations were checked, approver, and date.

evidence.claim: A model can turn a newly published text into a short brief with quotations. The brief is usable only after a person has checked every quotation against the official source.
FNV's September 2026 bargaining agenda asks, for the first time, for worker zeggenschap over AI and for AI-literacy training.
The CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer runs until 31 December 2026, which puts the 2027 round, including any AI clause, on the table now. The in-house warehouse CAO is bargained separately.
The works council discusses AI policy in the article 24 meeting, and one decision can require both advice and consent.

risks: A fluent brief with one wrong article number is repeated by payroll and by a site manager.
Filing the brief before the quotations are checked creates a false company position going into the CAO round.
The unions have put AI zeggenschap on the 2027 table, so a brief the OR has not seen can become the dispute.
research_questions: On the last two CAO or legal changes, how many hours went to finding the clause, and how many to deciding what Noordhaven would do?
In a trial on ten articles the team already knows, how often is a quotation wrong or attached to the wrong CAO?
Does the OR want the cited brief before the article 24 meeting, and does having it change the advice the OR gives?

tasks.short: Oversee how jobs are graded and keep the function house aligned with the work.

today.trigger: A vacancy for a new kind of role, a manager who says the job has outgrown its grade, or the periodic review of the function house.
steps: Collect the current job text and the manager's description of the work as it is done on the shift.
Compare both with the function group in the relevant CAO or the in-house function house.
Sit with the compensation specialist and the manager, and separate a changed job from a pay request for a person.
Set the grade and the pay band.
When the change affects pay or the house, take it to the OR before anyone updates AFAS.
drudgery: Pasting job texts into a comparison sheet.
Chasing managers for a description that matches the shift they actually run.
Repeating the comparison because flex and own staff do the same work under two texts.
today.time_sinks: Getting an honest description of the work takes longer than the grading meeting.

lenses.faster: Lining the old job text up against the manager's new text drops out. The grade conversation with the manager, and with the OR when pay would change, stays at its current length.
lenses.autonomous: It starts when a manager asks for a new role or says the work has changed, and at the yearly function-house review. A comparison draft is ready before the meeting; the director writes the grade.
lenses.ambitious: For the first time, grade the jobs that flex workers actually do on the night shift at each site, where the work has drifted from the written function group. Demand would grow if the comparison were cheap: supervisors change tasks every peak, and the compensation specialist cannot walk all three sites.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss pasting job texts into a sheet. The work to keep is the talk with the manager about what the shift really does, and with the OR when the grade would move pay.
lenses.options: Two comparisons of the same duties, one still inside the current function group and one outside it, change the pay band and whether the OR must consent. The grade follows that choice.
lenses.altitude: A regrade request arrives with the duties lined up against the function group and the gaps marked. The director keeps the right to set the grade, and gains a clearer split between a job that has changed and a person who wants higher pay. The expertise stays in the grading judgment and the OR conversation.
reach: The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's side-by-side of a job and a function group, once the director knows the function house and which changes require the works council's consent.

tasks.human_edge: The grade is pay and status. Two managers will describe the same job differently, and the director has to decide which description is the work. The OR's consent, where it applies, is given to a person, not to a draft.
tasks.pattern_why: The clerical comparison can be drafted, and the director stays the lead because the output is a grade for a job. A model score that proposed the grade would rate work the OR and the CAO treat as a pay decision, and it would be the heavier and riskier design.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks for a new role or says a job has changed, or the compensation specialist opens the yearly function-house review.
steps: The copilot places the manager's description next to the current function-group text and lists duties that appear in only one of them.
It lists facts still missing, such as night work, food safety, or supervision of flex.
The draft does not propose a grade and does not name an employee.
The director and the compensation specialist agree the facts with the manager.
The director sets the grade. If pay or the function group would change, the OR route is finished before AFAS is updated.
in_practice.human_gate: The director writes the grade. A change that moves pay or the function group waits for the works-council route the OR already has.
data_needed: Current function-group texts
The manager's description of the work
Whether own staff, flex, or both do that work
The pay band tied to the group
in_practice.logs_to: The function-house folder in SharePoint: the comparison, the missing facts, the grade the director signed, and the OR status.

evidence.claim: Dutch job grading compares the work to an agreed function group. The grade is a pay decision, and a description written to support a named person's rise is a different question from a change in the job.
Evaluation systems are in the high-risk employment list in the Commission draft, and a final human click does not take a tool that rates a worker outside that list.
The works council discusses AI in the article 24 meeting, and a decision can require both advice and consent, which is the route to clear before a grading aid is used on real jobs.

risks: If the draft names a person or suggests a grade, it rates the employee, and it may be an evaluation system under the AI Act from 2 December 2027.
Flex and own staff who do the same work can land in different groups if only the Noordhaven job text is compared.
A grade that moves pay, written into AFAS before the OR has consented, will be reversed in public.
research_questions: How many grade reviews in the last two years changed the function group, and how many were a pay request for a named person?
Does a side-by-side comparison, with no suggested grade, change the grade the director and the compensation specialist would have set?
Will the works council treat a draft comparison as an evaluation system under the AI Act text, even though the director writes the grade?

tasks.short: Forecast how many people the three sites need, fixed staff and flex.

today.trigger: The annual headcount plan, a budget round, or a warning from operations that a peak will need more flex than last season.
steps: Take current headcount and known leavers from AFAS.
Look at open roles in Recruitee and last year's 90-day retention by site.
Ask the three sites what agency capacity they expect, inside the seasonal range of 150 to 300 flex workers.
Build one forecast in Excel with the people analyst and FP&A.
Defend that single number to the finance director and to operations.
drudgery: Maintaining one workbook that tries to serve both operations and finance.
Reconciling agency orders with AFAS headcount.
Rewriting the forecast when one site moves its peak week.
today.time_sinks: The workbook and the reconciliation take the time, and the argument about the mix is squeezed to the end.

lenses.faster: Building and rebuilding the headcount sheet drops out. Choosing among three mixes with operations and the finance director still takes a meeting of about an hour each quarter.
lenses.autonomous: It starts at the quarterly operations meeting, and when a site asks to take the flex pool outside the seasonal range of 150 to 300. The three mixes are drafted from the people analyst's measures and the budget pack; the director chooses the mix that goes forward.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made each quarter, where today it is an annual spreadsheet: how much of the flex pool at each site to convert to Noordhaven contracts before peak, judged against that site's 90-day retention. Demand from operations would grow if the mixes were cheap to refresh, because each site manager asks again whenever a peak changes.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss maintaining the headcount workbook. The work to keep is the conversation with operations about what the peak really is, and whether last year's starters stayed past day 90.
lenses.options: Three mixes per site, hold the flex pool, convert part of it to fixed contracts, or hire fixed and release flex after the peak, change next year's cost and the chance that new people are still here at day 90. The mix taken into the room is the decision.
lenses.altitude: Before each quarterly operations meeting the director has three mixes, each with that site's 90-day retention. The director gains the right to take one mix to the finance director, and vacancies are opened only from that choice. The expertise moves toward the mix and the retention evidence; spreadsheet upkeep leaves the role.
reach: The FP&A Analyst's seasonal sketch of flex cost by site, once the director knows the rate cards in the three agency contracts and the people analyst's definition of 90-day retention.

tasks.human_edge: Operations will ask for more people before a peak. The director has to weigh that against starters who left before day 90 and against the agency mix. A headcount figure does not make that call, and it does not tell a site manager the answer.
tasks.pattern_why: The arithmetic can come from the budget program and the people analyst's measures, and the task itself is the choice of mix. A single calculated headcount would close that choice. The director stays the lead and takes one mix into the meeting.

in_practice.trigger: The quarterly operations meeting, and any request to take the flex pool outside the seasonal range of 150 to 300.
steps: The people analyst refreshes own staff, open roles, verzuim, and 90-day retention by site from the AFAS extract.
The copilot drafts three mixes per site: hold flex, convert part of the flex work to fixed contracts, or hire fixed and release flex after the peak.
Each mix shows the pay-cycle cost from the budget program and last year's 90-day retention for that site.
The director strikes any mix the volume data from operations does not support.
The director takes one mix to operations and the finance director. Vacancies in Recruitee start only after that choice.
in_practice.human_gate: The director chooses the mix that goes forward. A draft headcount is not a vacancy approval and does not start a search in Recruitee.
data_needed: Own staff and open roles by site
Flex hours by agency and site
90-day retention and verzuim by site
Peak volumes operations has already provided
in_practice.logs_to: The workforce-plan folder in SharePoint: the three mixes, the one chosen, and the vacancy approvals that follow.

evidence.claim: Workday's Work Intelligence, described as beta, reduced a planned 50 hires to 42 in a demo. That shows a planning aid producing one precise headcount, which is the outcome this task should keep as a scenario among others.

Noordhaven's flex pool already moves between about 150 and 300 people with the season. A forecast that ignores that range, or that ignores 90-day retention by site, answers a different question from the one operations and finance bring.

A tool that ranks which workers to hire or convert stays in the high-risk recruitment and evaluation category even when a person makes a final click. Counts by site and function group, with no score on a person, are a different design.

risks: A single generated headcount will be treated as the plan. The published demo that moved a plan from 50 hires to 42 shows how precise a draft number looks while it is still a demo.
A list of named flex workers to convert would be a selection tool, high-risk from 2 December 2027, and a final click does not exempt it.
Peak volume sits with operations. A forecast that uses only AFAS misses a lost or gained contract until the quarter is over.
research_questions: How far was last year's forecast from actual own staff and flex hours, by site and by month?
When operations and finance are shown three mixes tied to 90-day retention, do they approve a different mix from the single number they ask for today?
Which volume figures sit outside AFAS, and do they arrive in time for a quarterly choice?

role.altitude: The week moves from running the HR services to designing how they run: which steps an aid may take, where a person approves, what is logged, and what the works council has agreed. Manager satisfaction with HR, and the share of hires who are productive and still here at day 90, show whether that design works.
reach: The People Analytics and HRIS Analyst's monthly commentary on 90-day retention and verzuim, once the director can audit the measure definitions and the nightly AFAS extract.
The FP&A Analyst's first bridge from the personnel budget to AFAS actuals, once the director understands how the three agencies' invoices meet the ledger relative to the payroll close.
The Compensation and Benefits Specialist's first pass on a new CAO wage table, once the director can tell the transport scales from the in-house warehouse scales.
The Learning and Development Specialist's expiry list for forklift, VCA, and food safety, once the director knows which certificates each site requires.
role.ceiling_note: Supervising the team is already about 391 hours a year. Harassment, a stalled return under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, a dismissal, a bargaining session, and an OR dispute still need this person in the room. Three sites and a night shift cap how many of those conversations one director can hold. Every new aid adds gates and logs the OR can ask to see, and that review work grows with the number of aids.
skills_to_grow: Setting a gate per aid: what it may draft, what a person must approve, and when the works council's advice or consent comes first.
Reading the definitions of time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, and verzuim well enough to reject a bad figure.

The EU AI Act duties that apply now, including telling people when they are talking to a bot and training the HR team, and the high-risk duties for recruitment, monitoring, evaluation, and termination from 2 December 2027.
Bargaining AI zeggenschap and AI-literacy hours while the transport CAO is open through 31 December 2026, and the same subject in the in-house warehouse CAO.
Knowing which absence details are special-category data under the AVG and must stay out of prompts and out of OR packs.
role.ambitious_version: Across three sites the director spends the week on the calls only this role can make: whether a night-shift supervisor's problem is a policy answer or a real case, whether a site's 90-day retention means the next peak should be flex or fixed staff, and what the company will say to the unions about AI in the 2027 round. Routine status, routine policy answers, the budget arithmetic, and the first reading of a new text are prepared before the meeting. The twelve specialists keep the cases the aids are not allowed to close.
